passages.text: I am forever walking upon these shores, Betwixt the sand and the foam. The high tide will erase my foot-prints, And the wind will blow away the foam. But the sea and the shore will remain Forever.
passages.note: Transience of our traces; what endures

passages.text: It was but yesterday I thought myself a fragment quivering without rhythm in the sphere of life. Now I know that I am the sphere, and all life in rhythmic fragments moves within me.
passages.note: From feeling fragmentary to feeling whole

passages.text: They say to me in their awakening, “You and the world you live in are but a grain of sand upon the infinite shore of an infinite sea.” And in my dream I say to them, “I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are but grains of sand upon my shore.”
passages.note: Feeling small versus feeling vast inside

passages.text: Only once have I been made mute. It was when a man asked me, “Who are you?”
passages.note: Struggling to say who you really are

passages.text: A pearl is a temple built by pain around a grain of sand. What longing built our bodies and around what grains?
passages.note: Pain that builds something beautiful

passages.text: When God threw me, a pebble, into this wondrous lake I disturbed its surface with countless circles. But when I reached the depths I became very still.
passages.note: Restlessness on the surface, stillness in depth

passages.text: Give me silence and I will outdare the night.
passages.note: Silence as a source of courage

passages.text: I had a second birth when my soul and my body loved one another and were married.
passages.note: Making peace between body and soul

passages.text: Remembrance is a form of meeting. Forgetfulness is a form of freedom.
passages.note: Remembering and forgetting those we have lost

passages.text: Do not the spirits who dwell in the ether envy man his pain?
passages.note: Pain as something precious about being human

passages.text: On my way to the Holy City I met another pilgrim and I asked him, “Is this indeed the way to the Holy City?” And he said, “Follow me, and you will reach the Holy City in a day and a night.” And I followed him. And we walked many days and many nights, yet we did not reach the Holy City. And what was to my surprise he became angry with me because he had misled me.
passages.note: Being misled, then blamed by the one who misled

passages.text: Make me, oh God, the prey of the lion, ere You make the rabbit my prey.
passages.note: Preferring to be wronged than to wrong others

passages.text: One may not reach the dawn save by the path of the night.
passages.note: Hard times as the path to better ones

passages.text: My house says to me, “Do not leave me, for here dwells your past.” And the road says to me, “Come and follow me, for I am your future.” And I say to both my house and the road, “I have no past, nor have I a future. If I stay here, there is a going in my staying; and if I go there is a staying in my going. Only love and death change all things.”
passages.note: Torn between past and future; staying or going

passages.text: How can I lose faith in the justice of life, when the dreams of those who sleep upon feathers are not more beautiful than the dreams of those who sleep upon the earth?
passages.note: Trusting life's fairness; rich and poor alike dream

passages.text: Strange, the desire for certain pleasures is a part of my pain.
passages.note: Desire as part of suffering

passages.text: Seven times have I despised my soul: The first time when I saw her being meek that she might attain height. The second time when I saw her limping before the crippled. The third time when she was given to choose between the hard and the easy, and she chose the easy. The fourth time when she committed a wrong, and comforted herself that others also commit wrong. The fifth time when she forbore for weakness, and attributed her patience to strength. The sixth time when she despised the ugliness of a face, and knew not that it was one of her own masks. And the seventh time when she sang a song of praise, and deemed it a virtue.
passages.note: Honest self-examination of one's own failings

passages.text: I am ignorant of absolute truth. But I am humble before my ignorance and therein lies my honor and my reward.
passages.note: Humility about what we do not know

passages.text: There is a space between man's imagination and man's attainment that may only be traversed by his longing.
passages.note: Longing bridges dreams and achievement

passages.text: Paradise is there, behind that door, in the next room; but I have lost the key. Perhaps I have only mislaid it.
passages.note: Feeling locked out of happiness, with hope

passages.text: You are blind and I am deaf and dumb, so let us touch hands and understand.
passages.note: Understanding across differences and limitations

passages.text: The significance of man is not in what he attains, but rather in what he longs to attain.
passages.note: Worth lies in aspiration, not achievement

passages.text: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. And if it were not for the blackness of some of us, some of us would be dumb; And if it were not for the whiteness of some of us, some of us would be blind.
passages.note: Needing different kinds of people

passages.text: Give me an ear and I will give you a voice.
passages.note: Listening that gives others a voice

passages.text: Our mind is a sponge; our heart is a stream. Is it not strange that most of us choose sucking rather than running?
passages.note: Absorbing versus flowing through life

passages.text: When you long for blessings that you may not name, and when you grieve knowing not the cause, then indeed you are growing with all things that grow, and rising toward your greater self.
passages.note: Nameless longing and grief as growth

passages.text: When my cup is empty I resign myself to its emptiness; but when it is half full I resent its half-fulness.
passages.note: Dissatisfaction with having only half

passages.text: The reality of the other person is not in what he reveals to you, but in what he cannot reveal to you. Therefore, if you would understand him, listen not to what he says but rather to what he does not say.
passages.note: Understanding others through what they cannot say

passages.text: Half of what I say is meaningless; but I say it so that the other half may reach you.
passages.note: Imperfect words that still communicate

passages.text: A sense of humor is a sense of proportion.
passages.note: Humour and keeping perspective

passages.text: My loneliness was born when men praised my talkative faults and blamed my silent virtues.
passages.note: Loneliness from being valued for the wrong things

passages.text: A truth is to be known always, to be uttered sometimes.
passages.note: Knowing when to speak a truth

passages.text: The real in us is silent; the acquired is talkative.
passages.note: True self is quiet; the acquired is noisy

passages.text: The voice of life in me cannot reach the ear of life in you; but let us talk that we may not feel lonely.
passages.note: Talking to ease loneliness despite distance

passages.text: Only the dumb envy the talkative.
passages.note: Envy of those who speak easily

passages.text: If winter should say, “Spring is in my heart,” who would believe winter?
passages.note: Words that contradict how someone seems

passages.text: Should you really open your eyes and see, you would behold your image in all images. And should you open your ears and listen, you would hear your own voice in all voices.
passages.note: Seeing yourself in others

passages.text: It takes two of us to discover truth: one to utter it and one to understand it.
passages.note: Truth needs both speaker and listener

passages.text: Many a doctrine is like a window pane. We see truth through it but it divides us from truth.
passages.note: Beliefs that both reveal and divide

passages.text: Now let us play hide and seek. Should you hide in my heart it would not be difficult to find you. But should you hide behind your own shell, then it would be useless for anyone to seek you.
passages.note: Hiding behind defences makes us unreachable

passages.text: How noble is the sad heart who would sing a joyous song with joyous hearts.
passages.note: Joining others' joy while sad

passages.text: I would walk with all those who walk. I would not stand still to watch the procession passing by.
passages.note: Participating in life rather than watching

passages.text: You owe more than gold to him who serves you. Give him of your heart or serve him.
passages.note: Owing kindness, not just pay, to those who serve

passages.text: Trees are poems that the earth writes upon the sky. We fell them down and turn them into paper that we may record our emptiness.
passages.note: Wasting beauty on empty words

passages.text: If I were to choose between the power of writing a poem and the ecstasy of a poem unwritten, I would choose the ecstasy. It is better poetry.
passages.note: Valuing inner experience over achievement

passages.text: Poetry is not an opinion expressed. It is a song that rises from a bleeding wound or a smiling mouth.
passages.note: Art born from pain or joy

passages.text: If you sing of beauty though alone in the heart of the desert you will have an audience.
passages.note: Creating beauty even when alone

passages.text: Poetry is wisdom that enchants the heart. Wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
passages.note: Poetry and wisdom, heart and mind

passages.text: We often sing lullabyes to our children that we ourselves may sleep.
passages.note: Soothing others to soothe ourselves

passages.text: A great singer is he who sings our silences.
passages.note: Being understood without words

passages.text: How can you sing if your mouth be filled with food? How shall your hand be raised in blessing if it is filled with gold?
passages.note: Greed blocks generosity and joy

passages.text: They say the nightingale pierces his bosom with a thorn when he sings his love song. So do we all. How else should we sing?
passages.note: Love and creativity born of pain

passages.text: Even the most winged spirit cannot escape physical necessity.
passages.note: Limits of the body even for lofty spirits

passages.text: A madman is not less a musician than you or myself; only the instrument on which he plays is a little out of tune.
passages.note: Compassion for mental illness and difference

passages.text: The song that lies silent in the heart of a mother sings upon the lips of her child.
passages.note: What parents carry passes to children

passages.text: No longing remains unfulfilled.
passages.note: Hope that longing is never wasted

passages.text: I have never agreed with my other self wholly. The truth of the matter seems to lie between us.
passages.note: Inner conflict and finding the middle ground

passages.text: Your other self is always sorry for you. But your other self grows on sorrow; so all is well.
passages.note: Self-pity and growing through sorrow

passages.text: There is no struggle of soul and body save in the minds of those whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.
passages.note: Harmony of body and soul

passages.text: When you reach the heart of life you shall find beauty in all things, even in the eyes that are blind to beauty.
passages.note: Finding beauty everywhere

passages.text: We live only to discover beauty. All else is a form of waiting.
passages.note: Purpose: discovering beauty

passages.text: Sow a seed and the earth will yield you a flower. Dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you your beloved.
passages.note: Hope: dreams bring what we love

passages.text: The devil died the very day you were born. Now you do not have to go through hell to meet an angel.
passages.note: Fresh start without needing suffering

passages.text: If you would possess you must not claim.
passages.note: Love without possessiveness

passages.text: When a man’s hand touches the hand of a woman they both touch the heart of eternity.
passages.note: The sacredness of touch between lovers

passages.text: Love is the veil between lover and lover.
passages.note: Love itself as a veil between lovers
